nodes.label: IngestionService
nodes.rationale: Deduplicates in flight, counts, and publishes through the EventPublisher port. Swapping the in-memory bus for Kafka changed nothing in it, which is the point of the port.

nodes.label: The Normalized Event Envelope
nodes.rationale: source and producer both exist because they answer different debugging questions — after a provider swap, source is the only thing that says which rows came from where. Money is Decimal and always a string in JSON, because a JSON number becomes an IEEE-754 double in every JavaScript client there is.

nodes.label: Provider Adapters (synthetic / replay / alpaca)
nodes.rationale: Nothing above the adapter knows a vendor exists; the test for it is that swapping TW_PROVIDER changes one line of configuration and nothing else. Setting a provider without its credentials fails at startup, because an auth failure hours later in a stack trace that does not mention environment variables is a bad way to learn you forgot one.

nodes.label: SyntheticScenario Failure Injection
nodes.rationale: The synthetic provider does something real data cannot: produce a specific failure on demand — dropped socket, malformed frames, duplicate prints, volume spikes, and a connected-but-silent stall. Its distributions are invented, so it proves the pipeline works, never that a strategy works.

nodes.label: Ingestion Resilience Policy
nodes.rationale: Bad credentials are not retryable because a bad key does not become good on the fourth attempt and retrying burns the rate-limit budget to learn nothing. Malformed messages are never retried because the same bytes parse the same way. Quotes are shed before trades: losing a quote costs a tick of book detail, losing a trade corrupts the tape. Cancellation propagates immediately or shutdown hangs.

nodes.label: Full Jitter Backoff
nodes.rationale: sleep = random(0, min(cap, base × 2^attempt)). Fixed backoff makes every client retry in lockstep, so a provider recovering from an outage is immediately hit by a synchronised herd. The attempt counter resets after any successful message so a week of uptime does not inherit an old outage's backoff.

nodes.label: StalenessMonitor
nodes.rationale: Watches per-symbol gaps including symbols that have never sent anything, which is how a failed subscription is caught. A connected-but-silent stall is the nasty failure.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Deduplication
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE(event_id) in PostgreSQL is the guarantee because it is a fact about stored rows, correct across restarts and replicas. The in-flight window is only an optimisation and deliberately forgets — an unbounded set would add no correctness in exchange for a memory leak that grows with every tick. Both only work because event ids are deterministic.

nodes.label: IngestionStats Counters
nodes.rationale: Every failure path increments a counter and every counter is asserted on by a test, which makes 'do not silently discard errors' checkable rather than aspirational.

edges.source_location: both bound a synchronised storm (herd vs alert storm)
